title: Pindar, the four books of victory odes (Olympian, Pythian, Nemean, Isthmian), in Sandys's Greek (Loeb Classical Library)

license.payload: Pindar is public domain. Sandys's Greek text (The Odes of Pindar, Loeb Classical Library, 1915; the Perseus file follows the 1937 printing) is public domain in the European Union (Sandys died 1922). The TEI is the Perseus Digital Library's, CC BY-SA 4.0, redistributed under the same licence and attributed to Perseus.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

normalization: Originals as fetched under original/, pinned to a commit of the repository named in origin.items. text/<slug>.txt is the TEI reduced to plain text by seat.py (rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-27), notes and apparatus dropped, divisions kept. No text was corrected by hand.

scope: The four books of epinicians entire. The fragments (paeans, dithyrambs, partheneia, threnoi) are not in the Perseus files; they are queued to Bergk's Poetae Lyrici Graeci, 4th edition, vol. I (1878).
why_seated: Pindar is the ninth of the nine lyric poets and the only one whose books survive; the seat carries the canon whose other members survive in fragments.

research.study: The Portents Before the Fall: Josephus, Tacitus and the Apocalypse (#1737) and the Sappho line (Sappho 31, the reception operator of #1494–#1495)
